questions.q: How does propeller thrust depend on RPM, all else being equal?
questions.explain: Ct = T/(ρ·n²·D⁴): thrust grows with the square of RPM, power with the cube.

questions.q: Why is a big slow prop more efficient than a small fast one at the same thrust?
options: It has more blades and less pitch
A slow, large flow is cheaper in energy
It runs at a lower voltage
questions.explain: Thrust ~ flow momentum (~V), power ~ kinetic energy (~V²): a lot of air moved slowly is cheaper.

questions.q: What happens to thrust at the same RPM in the mountains?
options: It drops: the motor is colder and weaker
questions.explain: F = ½·ρ·A·(Vₑ²−V₀²): thrust is proportional to air density ρ.

questions.q: By what factor must power increase to double thrust (ideal model)?
What does “7×3.5×3” mean in a prop designation?
questions.explain: Diameter in inches, pitch in inches, number of blades.

questions.q: What is the main document when choosing a motor-prop combo?
options: Store reviews and photos of the motor
questions.explain: Prop, voltage, throttle → thrust, current, g/W: you use it to calculate the hover operating point, T/W and flight time.

questions.q: In an X8, the total thrust of a coaxial pair compared with two single props is:
options: The same, the flows don't interfere
questions.explain: The lower prop works in the swirled, accelerated flow of the upper one and loses part of its thrust.

questions.q: What is the thrust coefficient Cₜ?
options: The ratio of pitch to diameter
questions.explain: Cₜ lets you compare props independently of RPM and size.
